---
title: "🏊‍♂️🚴‍♀️🏃 Triathlon Training Calendar"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    page-layout: full
    toc: false
    theme: none
params:
  data_file: "workouts.json"
  year: 2026
  month: 9
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r setup}

# params <- list(data_file = "workouts.json", year = 2026, month = 9)

source("functions.R")
source("global_vars.R")

workouts <- params$data_file |>
  jsonlite::fromJSON(simplifyDataFrame = TRUE) |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(date),
    completed = as.logical(completed)
  )

first_day <- as.Date(
  sprintf(
    "%04d-%02d-01",
    as.integer(params$year),
    as.integer(params$month)
  )
)

last_day <- lubridate::ceiling_date(first_day, "month") - lubridate::days(1)

lead_blanks <- wday_sun(first_day) - 1

trail_blanks <- (7 - wday_sun(last_day)) %% 7

month_dates <- seq(first_day, last_day, by = "day")

all_cells <- as.Date(
  c(
    rep(NA_real_, lead_blanks),
    as.numeric(month_dates),
    rep(NA_real_, trail_blanks)
  ),
  origin = "1970-01-01"
)


n_weeks <- length(all_cells) / 7
week_rows <- vapply(
  seq_len(n_weeks),
  function(w) {
    idx <- ((w - 1) * 7 + 1):(w * 7)
    paste0(
      '<div class="cal-row">',
      paste(
        vapply(all_cells[idx], build_day_cell, character(1)),
        collapse = ""
      ),
      '</div>'
    )
  },
  character(1)
)

month_label <- format(first_day, "%B %Y")
```

```{r render-calendar}
#| output: asis

calendar <- paste0(readLines("html/calendar.html"), collapse = "\n")

calendar <- glue::glue(
  calendar,
  month_label = month_label,
  week_rows = paste(week_rows, collapse = ""),
  .open = "{{",
  .close = "}}",
  .trim = FALSE
)

cat("```{=html}\n", calendar, "\n```\n", sep = "")
```

```{r monthly-summary}
#| output: asis
month_totals <- workouts |>
  dplyr::filter(date >= first_day, date <= last_day) |>
  dplyr::group_by(sport) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    minutes = sum(duration_min, na.rm = TRUE),
    sessions = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


cards <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(month_totals)),
  function(i) {
    row <- month_totals[i, ]
    meta <- get_meta(row$sport)
    bg <- card_colors[[row$sport]]
    if (is.null(bg)) {
      bg <- "#334155"
    }
    paste0(
      '<div class="summary-card" style="background:',
      bg,
      '">',
      '<span class="big">',
      meta$icon,
      ' ',
      row$minutes,
      '</span>',
      '<span class="lbl">',
      meta$label,
      ' min &middot; ',
      row$sessions,
      ' sessions</span>',
      '</div>'
    )
  },
  character(1)
)

cat(paste0(
  '<div class="summary-panel">',
  paste(cards, collapse = ""),
  '</div>'
))
```

```{r upcoming}
#| output: asis
upcoming <- workouts |>
  dplyr::filter(date >= Sys.Date(), date <= Sys.Date() + lubridate::days(6)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(date)

if (nrow(upcoming) > 0) {
  items <- vapply(
    seq_len(nrow(upcoming)),
    function(i) {
      w <- upcoming[i, ]
      meta <- get_meta(w$sport)
      paste0(
        '<li><span class="u-date">',
        format(w$date, "%a %b %d"),
        '</span>',
        '<span class="u-chip ',
        meta$class,
        '">',
        meta$icon,
        ' ',
        meta$label,
        '</span>',
        '<span>',
        html_escape(w$title),
        ' (',
        w$duration_min,
        ' min)</span></li>'
      )
    },
    character(1)
  )
  cat(paste0(
    '<div class="upcoming"><h3>&#x1F4C5; Next 7 Days</h3><ul>',
    paste(items, collapse = ""),
    '</ul></div>'
  ))
} else {
  cat(paste0(
    '<div class="upcoming"><h3>&#x1F4C5; Next 7 Days</h3>',
    '<p>No workouts scheduled &mdash; add some to <code>workouts.json</code>.</p></div>'
  ))
}
```

<!--
HOW TO USE
----------
1. Put this file and workouts.json in the same folder, then render:
     quarto render workout-calendar.qmd

2. To view a different month, render with params, e.g. for July 2026:
     quarto render workout-calendar.qmd -P year:2026 -P month:7

   Or duplicate this file per month and hardcode `year`/`month` in the YAML
   if you want a set of monthly pages you click between.

3. Add workouts by appending objects to workouts.json:
     {"date": "2026-11-02", "sport": "bike", "title": "Zone 2 ride",
      "duration_min": 60, "intensity": "easy", "notes": "", "completed": false}

   Valid `sport` values (each has its own color): swim, bike, run, strength, rest, race.
   Any other value still renders (as a gray chip) so nothing breaks if you add a new type.

4. Hover any workout chip to see its full title, duration, and notes as a tooltip.
   Today's date gets a dashed orange outline; the "Next 7 Days" panel below the
   calendar is a quick planning list independent of which month is displayed above.
-->
